Le embolie piccole si perdono quando si:
Small emboli are missed when only the center is examined. The method: for each lobe, follow the lobar artery and every segmental branch out to the periphery, scrolling back and forth with a wide window (100/700) and, when in doubt, with MPR along the vessel or a thin MIP. A true thrombus is a defect within the lumen, recognizable on several consecutive images; the most common false positives are hilar lymph nodes (outside the vessel), mixing-flow artifacts (blurred edges, which disappear with windowing), respiratory motion and veins mistaken for arteries (arteries run next to the bronchi).

Even an isolated segmental embolism is a finding to communicate immediately: in the absence of contraindications it is treated with anticoagulants. The case is also a localization exercise: mark the thrombus on the image.
